data.exact_reserve_text: Within the calendar year technical result, a deficit of GBP 5.2m (2016: surplus of GBP 0.8m) relates to the reassessment of net claims incurred for previous accident years.
specific_events: Investment group life contract (mandatory group scheme - investment scheme)

prior_year_events.event_name: UNFCU group life policy licensing breach
prior_year_events.impact_description: Licensing breach discovered with concentration of US lives led to regulatory action and an estimated actuarial liability being recognised on the 2016 year of account.
Mandatory group scheme underwriting proved not to be mandatory, resulting in higher than expected sales volume and a reserved unexpired risks provision reflecting adverse expected loss ratios.

named_events.event_name: UNFCU group life policy licensing breach
named_events.loss_description: Estimated actuarial liability of GBP 7.7m booked on the 2016 year of account for the licensing breach; subsequently signed forward into 2018 year of account.

Contract reserved at a loss ratio of approximately 200% on a forecast ultimate premium, net of commissions, of GBP 8.9m split across the 2016 and 2017 years of account; resulted in an unexpired risks provision of GBP 8.6m.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 308 opened 2017 with gross long-term business provisions of GBP 10.925m. During 2017 the syndicate recorded adverse prior-year reassessments (a net deficit of GBP 5.2m) driven principally by life book specific issues: a licensing breach on a UNFCU group life policy (actuarial liability ~GBP 7.7m) and a poorly-performing investment-group life contract that required an unexpired risks provision (~GBP 8.6m). An additional expense reserve (~GBP 1.1m) was also established to cover long-term maintenance costs. Overall the prior year movement represents a material reserve strengthening concentrated in the long-term (life) book.
raw_causal_phrases: Within the calendar year technical result, a deficit of GBP 5.2m (2016: surplus of GBP 0.8m) relates to the reassessment of net claims incurred for previous accident years.
The largest was the recognition of an unexpired risks provision of GBP 8.6m resulting from the aforementioned investment group life contract.
The second was the estimated actuarial liability of GBP 7.7m in relation to the UNFCU policy.

The third was the establishment of an additional expense reserve of GBP 1.1m to cover the future costs associated with maintaining the long-term contracts, which has been included as part of the long-term business provision.

Although some growth was possible, there was an increase in claims frequency on key binders and a higher expense ratio, in part caused by increased costs of managing the business through delegated authorities, regulation and compliance.
data.data_quality_notes: Gross prior-year development (PYD) was not presented explicitly. The report explicitly states a NET prior-year deficit of GBP 5.2m (used here as fallback). No gross PYD figure in the 'Insurance liabilities' column was found; reconciliation and notes show gross long-term provision movements (opening 10.925m to closing 20.986m) and event-specific gross amounts (7.7m, 8.6m). Opening reserves taken from the balance sheet 'long-term business provision' prior-year column. Claims development triangle is present and used as supplemental data, but an explicit gross PYD movement line was not provided, so net figure was used and flagged.
